headline: Postponed Pawtucket teachers' contract for 2026 through 2029 and recommended approval of a Parking Enforcement Officer pay ordinance.
summary: Members postponed the teacher contract so the School Department can answer their questions. The questions covered surplus medical funds, class size, teacher absences, and the contract's longevity language. The committee also recommended approval of an ordinance adding the Parking Enforcement Officer to the Local 3960 pay rates.
decisions: Placed on file the communication requesting approval to establish a Parking Enforcement Officer position.
Recommended approval 3-0 of the ordinance repealing and replacing the Local 3960 pay rate schedule to add the Parking Enforcement Officer.
Postponed the Pawtucket Teachers' Alliance contract for September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2029 to give the School Department time to answer questions.

decision_titles: Request to establish Parking Enforcement Officer position
Pay rate schedule for Local 3960, adding Parking Enforcement Officer
plain_text:
PAWTUCKET CITY COUNCIL 
FINANCE COMMITTEE  
SEPTEMBER 23, 2026 
 
A meeting of the City Council Finance Committee was held on Wednesday, September 23, 
2026, at 6:01 p.m., in the Temporary City Council Office, Room 204, 2nd Floor, 100 Freight 
Street, Pawtucket, RI. 
 
Present - Councilor Wildenhain, Chair; Councilors Moran and Rubio. 
 
Absent – 0. 
 
Councilor Wildenhain presided. 
 
Also present were Council President Mercer; Gregg Anderson, Human Resources Coordinator; 
Major Ken Dolan, Pawtucket Police Department; Jo anne Bonollo, Chair, Pawtucket School 
Committee; James Chellel, Jr., Pawtucket School Committee; Stephanie DeMaio, Chief 
Financial Officer, Pawtucket School Department; and Carey Edwards, Controller, Pawtucket 
School Department. 
 
The Committee conducted a public input period, at which there were no speakers. 
 
The Committee took up the following: 
 
Communication from Gregg T. Anderson , Human Resources Coordinator, to the Honorable 
Members of the Pawtucket  City Council (Request for City Council Approval and Personnel 
Board Recommendation – Establishment of Parking Enforcement Officer Position) 
 
This communication was READ AND ORDERED FILED. 
 
 
The Committee took up the following: 
 
AN ORDINANCE REPEALING AND REPLACING THE SCHEDULE OF PAY RATES 
FOR LOCAL 3960 IN SECTION §88 -12 OF THE CODE OF ORDINANCES OF THE CITY 
OF PAWTUCKET, 1996 (Add: Parking Enforcement Officer)  
 
Mr. Anderson read the communication he presented to the Council and stated that Major Dolan 
was present to answer any questions. 
 
Major Dolan stated that the Parking Enforcement Officer would be the only officer who would 
mainly handle parking issues and could request help if needed .  He stated that the shifts would 
be flexible based on what was happening in the City. 
 
Upon motion made by Councilor Rubio, seconded by Councilor Moran, the Committee 
recommended APPROVAL of this ordinance on a roll call vote, as follows: 
 
AYES – Councilor Wildenhain, Chair; Councilors Moran and Rubio 
 
NOES – 0.
Finance Committee 
September 23, 2026 
Page 2 
 
The Committee took up the following: 
 
Contract between the Pawtucket School Committee and the Pawtucket Teachers’ 
Alliance, Local 930, A.F.T., A.F.L.-C.I.O., for the period beginning September 1, 2026 through 
August 31, 2029 
 
Ms. DeMaio explained that the teachers agreed to ten additional teaching minutes the first year 
for the added education time required by RIDE, and five minutes in each of the next two years .  
The salary increases are 3.0% for the first year, 3.0/1.25% in the second year and 2.0/1.75% in 
the third year. 
 
The School Department ha s a surplus of $4.1 million in medical reserves, but wanted to keep 
some.  With school committee approval, t hey may use up to 75%  of the surplus , but only t o 
offset the premiums.   
 
She stated that more money would not be needed in this year’s budget.   
 
Ms. DeMaio stated that the regular education class size will be  down in the first year and 
special education class size will be down in years 2 and 3. 
 
Ms. Bonollo stated that they would hire a master planner for school use and are down 3,000 
students since she started.  The dual language classes are not in this budget. 
 
Ms. DeMaio stated that they have longevity in the bu dget and there are two new layers that 
incentivizes people to stay. 
 
Councilor Wildenhain asked the following questions: 
 
• How many employees are there in the school department, all inclusive? 
• How many employees are in this contract? 
• To date, what is the total school department surplus? 
• Is there a 5-year projection for the school department? 
• How d oes the school department plan to cover the $17 million increase in the new 
contract? 
• He requested a c larification on Section 24, Certified/Licensed Personnel Safet y and 
Protection from Harassment – the right to leave a meeting in which prohibited behavior 
occurred. 
 
Councilor Rubio asked: 
 
• Are there any financial risks or obligations beyond the term of this contract being 
projected?
Finance Committee 
September 23, 2026 
Page 3 
 
President Mercer asked the following questions: 
 
• Is Section 3, Class Size., new in this contract? 
- Ms. DiMaio responded that it was in the contract, then taken out, and is now back 
in. 
• How are students dispersed when a teacher is absent and the re is no substitute teacher 
available?  How are they reassigned?   How much does dispersing/reassigning  students 
cost?   
• Pawtucket has one of the highest rates of teacher absenteeism in the state.   How much 
does this absenteeism cost? 
• How many teachers are not Right to Read certified? 
- Ms. Bonollo responded 43. 
• The school department  is using $3 million of their medical surplus to offset this year’s 
deficit. D oes that mean there will be a $5.4 million deficit in the 2 nd year of the 
contract? 
• What is the new longevity language setting the school department up for after 2029? 
 
In response to President Mercer’s comment that the school committee approved the budget 
after about 15 minutes of discussion in executive session, Mr. Chellel responded that the 
School Committee had addressed the budget in executive session for over an hour. 
 
Upon motion made by Councilor Moran, seconded by Councilor Rubio, the Committee 
POSTPONED this matter to give the School Department appropriate time to answer the 
questions and scheduled a meeting for the Committee of the Whole and Finance Committee for 
Monday, September 28, 2026. 
 
The meeting was adjourned at 6:51 p.m. 
 
 
 
Richard J. Goldstein, MMC, City Clerk 
Pawtucket City Council
